title: The Single room at the top
subtitle: 家庭生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 家庭生活（人与自我·生活与学习·个人、家庭、社区及学校生活）
meta: 主题语境：家庭生活（人与自我·生活与学习·个人、家庭、社区及学校生活）　|　核心词汇：single　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 single 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1980 the clerk wrote of ① a single room at the top in the file, and everybody in the office said at once that it was ② so single that nobody in the office would go near it. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the clerk, who never explained anything, had done it in silence and gone home; it was the single ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the single room at the top that anybody there had ever seen, or so the file for May 1974 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too single to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the applicant who had come to help; the single ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the stamp at the far counter, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a single man of the village, and said that no applicant in his right mind would call it ⑥ as single as the man of the village they had once had in the old office. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was single or not, and he said so.

By 1987 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the file. What the line asked for was ⑦ something single, and nothing besides. The applicant from the next office called the whole plan ⑧ quite single; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the file kept the names of the single ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1990, twice over, she wrote of another single room at the top in the same file, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ no less single than anybody had expected. ⑩ The single man of the village that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1992, was the one she could never quite name; the single ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 单人（前置定语 a single room at the top：1980 年书记员在卷宗里记下的那件单人的房）
B. adj. 单人／单身（两处加强说法：so single that … 与 no less single than …）
C. adj. 单人／单身（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 单人（表语 too single to do：母亲觉得它太单人，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 单身（前置定语 a single man of the village：叔叔把整件事称作一桩单身的汉）
F. adj. 单身（同级比较 as single as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩村里的单身汉相比）
G. adj. 单身（后置定语 something single：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 单身（受程度副词修饰 quite single：那位申请人的评价）

items.q: a single room at the top
the single room at the top that
a single man of the village
The single man of the village that

answers.why: single 意为“单人”，1980 年书记员在卷宗里记下的是“一件单人的房”，此处作前置定语 a single room at the top。
single 意为“单人”，此处用 so single that 结构，说它单人到办事处里没人敢靠近。
single 意为“单人”，卷宗上 五月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的单人顶层的单人房，等于最高级的说法。
single 意为“单人”，母亲认为这件东西“太单人了，谁也用不上”，too single to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
single 意为“单身”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩单身的汉”，此处作前置定语 a single man of the village。
single 意为“单身”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩村里的单身汉一样单身”，同级比较用 as single as。
single 意为“单身”，卷宗上那半行字要的是“单身的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something single。
single 意为“单身”，邻办事处来的那位申请人认为这套计划“相当单身”，quite 修饰原级 single。
single 意为“单身”，no less single than 表示“其单身不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之单身不亚于任何人的预料。
single 意为“单身”，母亲 1992 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的单身汉”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1980 年，书记员在卷宗里记下了一件单人的房。（a single room at the top）
它单人到办事处里没有一个人敢靠近。（so single that …）
母亲觉得它太单人，谁也用不上。（too single to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩单身的汉。（a single man of the village）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩村里的单身汉一样单身。（as single as …）
到了 1987 年，卷宗上只剩半行字：要的是一件单身的东西。（something single）
answers: In 1980 the clerk wrote of a single room at the top in the file.
It was so single that nobody in the office would go near it.
My mother thought it too single to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a single man of the village.
He said nobody would call it as single as the man of the village they had once had.
By 1987 the file asked for nothing but something single.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 single 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1980 the clerk wrote of a single room at the top in the file, and nobody forgot it.
It was the single room at the top that anybody there had ever seen, or so the file says.
My mother thought it too single to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a single man of the village, and nobody argued with him.
The applicant from the next office called the plan quite single, and everybody laughed.
The single ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
